description: Check whether the Zoopla API is available.
Turn typed text into the location_id every search takes: towns, areas, postcode districts, postcodes, streets, stations and schools.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
**What the user is typing**  -  a town, city, area, postcode district, full postcode, station or
school name. Required; 2 to 100 characters.

Partial words work (`manch` finds Manchester), a postcode district returns itself (`nw3` →
`nw3`, labelled "Hampstead, Belsize Park, Swiss Cottage"), and a full or partial postcode (`NW8 0RE`,
`m19 2`) returns postcode locations. Each row carries the `location_id` every search takes.

Punctuation and accents are forgiven: `king's lynn`, `newcastle-upon-tyne`, `st. albans`, `Leeds, West
Yorkshire` (a pasted label) and `Flat 1/2 High St` all search normally. A query with nothing searchable
left (`..`, `//`) answers `count: 0`, never an error.

parameters.name: include_addresses
parameters.description:
**Also return matching street addresses with their UPRNs, and street locations.** Optional;
default off.

`true` adds `addresses` (up to 10, each `uprn`, `address`, `latitude`, `longitude`) and
`addresses_total` (how many addresses match in all; it stops counting at 10,000), and adds matching
streets to `results` as `kind: "street"` rows (e.g. `reading/manchester-road`). Type a house number
and street (`10 downing street`) to find a property: pass its `uprn` to the property endpoints.
Postcode-shaped queries always include postcode locations, with or without this flag.

description: Every residential address at a UK postcode, each with its UPRN.

parameters.name: postcode
parameters.description:
**A full UK postcode.** Required.

Case and the space are optional: `M19 2AB`, `m192ab` and `m19 2ab` are the same postcode, and so is its
`location_id` from `/locations` or `/search` (`m19-2ab`). A value
that is not a full postcode (a district such as `M19`, a partial `M19 2`) is a 400  -  use
`/locations` to complete a partial postcode first. A well-formed postcode with no residential
addresses on record (business-only or retired postcodes, e.g. `SW1A 1AA`) is a 404.

description: The postcode, district, town and region at a UK map point, with location_ids to search around it.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the point, in decimal degrees.** Required; UK only  -  `49` to `61`.

`51.5074` is central London, `53.4808` central Manchester, `55.9533` Edinburgh. Pair it with
`longitude`. A point outside the UK box, or in the Republic of Ireland or France (both inside it)  -  on land or
in their waters: the Irish half of the Irish Sea, and the sea within a few km of the French coast  -  is a 400; a
blank value is a 400, never read as `0`.

description: Search UK homes for sale, to rent, new homes and commercial property in a place, with the full filter set, four sorts and pages of 25.

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description:
**The place to search.** Required.

Take the `location_id` from any row of `/locations` (the autocomplete) or from `/location-by-coordinates`
(`postcode_location_id` / `outcode_location_id`). Ids are readable slugs:

- `manchester`, `london`, `uk`  -  a town, city, county or the whole country.
- `hampstead`, `manchester-city-centre`  -  an area or neighbourhood.
- `nw3`, `m19`  -  a postcode district (outcode).
- `nw8-0re`  -  a full postcode (a pasted `NW8 0RE` or `NW80RE` is accepted and read as `nw8-0re`).
- `reading/manchester-road`  -  a street.
- `station/rail/manchester-piccadilly`, `schools/secondary/manchester-academy`  -  the area around a station
  or school (searched as a ½-mile circle unless `radius` says otherwise).

Case and surrounding slashes are forgiven. A value that is not slug-shaped is a **400**; a well-formed id
that names no Zoopla location is a **404**.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description:
**Which market to search.** Optional; default `for-sale`.

- `for-sale`  -  homes for sale (the default).
- `to-rent`  -  homes to rent.
- `new-homes`  -  new-build homes for sale (every new home counts as chain free).
- `commercial-for-sale`  -  commercial property for sale (offices, shops, hospitality, industrial, land).
- `commercial-to-rent`  -  commercial property to let.

**Filters are per section**  -  one outside its section is a 400 naming the sections that take it:

- **Every section:** price, floor area, `property_type`, `keywords`, `added`, `smart_tags`, `feature`,
  `reduced_price_only`; `radius` for a named place.
- **Residential:** bedrooms and bathrooms.
- **Sale:** `tenure`, `include_sold`, `is_auction`; `chain_free` (not `new-homes`); `is_shared_ownership`,
  `is_retirement_home`, `is_development`, `buyer_incentive` (`for-sale`, `new-homes`); `new_homes` (`for-sale`).
- **Letting:** `price_frequency`, `furnished_state`, `rental_term`, `include_rented`, `bills_included`,
  `pets_allowed`, `available_now`; `is_shared_accommodation`, `is_student_accommodation`, `is_retirement_home`
  (`to-rent`); `tenure` (`commercial-to-rent`).

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description:
**Lowest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `200000`  -  £200k and up for sale.
- `1000`  -  £1,000 a month and up to rent.

Both bounds are inclusive. `price_min` greater than `price_max` is a 400. Every row carries its numeric `price`, so the bound can be checked row by row (POA listings have `price: null`).

- `0`  -  studios included (it still drops the few listings that state no bedroom count).
- `3`  -  three bedrooms or more.
- `11`  -  eleven or more.

commercial sections: almost no commercial listing states bedrooms, so it would exclude nearly all of them.

parameters.name: property_type
parameters.description:
**Kind of property.** Optional; one value or several comma-separated  -  **several are combined (any of
them)**, e.g. `detached,semi_detached` or `industrial,warehouse`.

**Residential sections** (`for-sale`, `to-rent`, `new-homes`):

- `houses`  -  detached, semi-detached and terraced; or `detached`, `semi_detached`, `terraced` alone
  (detached bungalows count as detached).
- `bungalow`, or the finer `detached_bungalow`, `semi_detached_bungalow`, `terraced_bungalow`.
- `cottage`, `barn_conversion`.
- `flats`  -  flats, apartments and maisonettes; `studio`  -  studio flats only.
- `park_home`  -  park and mobile homes; `land`  -  land and plots; `farms_land`  -  land plus farms.
- `hotel`, `hospitality`, `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `retail`, `offices`, `industrial`, `light_industrial`,
  `warehouse`  -  a hotel, shop or office sold or let with living space.

**Commercial sections:**

- `offices`, `serviced_office` (part of `offices`), `retail` (shops).
- `hospitality` (restaurants, pubs, hotels, leisure), or `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `hotel` alone.
- `industrial`, `light_industrial`, `warehouse`; `land`, `farms_land` (land and sites).

A value outside the section's list is a 400 naming the accepted ones. Leisure units, car parking and
business parks have no filter of their own.

parameters.description:

  other `%` is searched as typed.

and page each slice. A page past 40 is a 400.

location_id.description:
**The place to search.** Required.

Take the `location_id` from any row of `/locations` (the autocomplete) or from `/location-by-coordinates`
(`postcode_location_id` / `outcode_location_id`). Ids are readable slugs:

- `manchester`, `london`, `uk`  -  a town, city, county or the whole country.
- `hampstead`, `manchester-city-centre`  -  an area or neighbourhood.
- `nw3`, `m19`  -  a postcode district (outcode).
- `nw8-0re`  -  a full postcode (a pasted `NW8 0RE` or `NW80RE` is accepted and read as `nw8-0re`).
- `reading/manchester-road`  -  a street.
- `station/rail/manchester-piccadilly`, `schools/secondary/manchester-academy`  -  the area around a station
  or school (searched as a ½-mile circle unless `radius` says otherwise).

Case and surrounding slashes are forgiven. A value that is not slug-shaped is a **400**; a well-formed id
that names no Zoopla location is a **404**.

section.description:
**Which market to search.** Optional; default `for-sale`.

- `for-sale`  -  homes for sale (the default).
- `to-rent`  -  homes to rent.
- `new-homes`  -  new-build homes for sale (every new home counts as chain free).
- `commercial-for-sale`  -  commercial property for sale (offices, shops, hospitality, industrial, land).
- `commercial-to-rent`  -  commercial property to let.

**Filters are per section**  -  one outside its section is a 400 naming the sections that take it:

- **Every section:** price, floor area, `property_type`, `keywords`, `added`, `smart_tags`, `feature`,
  `reduced_price_only`; `radius` for a named place.
- **Residential:** bedrooms and bathrooms.
- **Sale:** `tenure`, `include_sold`, `is_auction`; `chain_free` (not `new-homes`); `is_shared_ownership`,
  `is_retirement_home`, `is_development`, `buyer_incentive` (`for-sale`, `new-homes`); `new_homes` (`for-sale`).
- **Letting:** `price_frequency`, `furnished_state`, `rental_term`, `include_rented`, `bills_included`,
  `pets_allowed`, `available_now`; `is_shared_accommodation`, `is_student_accommodation`, `is_retirement_home`
  (`to-rent`); `tenure` (`commercial-to-rent`).

price_min.description:
**Lowest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `200000`  -  £200k and up for sale.
- `1000`  -  £1,000 a month and up to rent.

Both bounds are inclusive. `price_min` greater than `price_max` is a 400. Every row carries its numeric `price`, so the bound can be checked row by row (POA listings have `price: null`).

price_max.description:
**Highest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no ceiling when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `300000`  -  up to £300k for sale.
- `1200`  -  up to £1,200 a month to rent (`1200` with `price_frequency=per_week` means £1,200 a week).

Send it with `price_min` for a band. Price bands are also the best way to split a big search into
slices of under 1,000 listings each (see `page`). At least `1`: Zoopla reads `0` as no ceiling, so it
is refused rather than silently returning everything.

price_frequency.description:
**The unit `price_min` / `price_max` are read in, for rentals.** Optional; default `per_month`.

- `per_month`  -  monthly rent (pcm).
- `per_week`  -  weekly rent (pw): `price_max=250&price_frequency=per_week` ≈ £1,083 a month.
- `per_year`  -  annual rent (pa), how commercial rents are usually quoted: `price_max=12000&price_frequency=per_year`
  = £1,000 a month.

It changes only how the price bounds are read  -  rows still show each listing's own advertised price and `price_frequency`. Accepted with `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent` only.

beds_min.description:
**Fewest bedrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647). Residential sections only.

- `0`  -  studios included (it still drops the few listings that state no bedroom count).
- `3`  -  three bedrooms or more.
- `11`  -  eleven or more.

Each row reports its own `bedrooms`. `beds_min` greater than `beds_max` is a 400. Not accepted on
commercial sections: almost no commercial listing states bedrooms, so it would exclude nearly all of them.

beds_max.description:
**Most bedrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647), except `10`.

- `0`  -  studios, plus any room let listed with `0` bedrooms.
- `2`  -  up to two bedrooms.

Send with `beds_min` for an exact count (`beds_min=2&beds_max=2`). `10` is a 400: Zoopla reads it as its
"10+" option (no ceiling), so no value caps a search at exactly 10  -  send `9` or `11`. Not accepted on
commercial sections.

baths_min.description:
**Fewest bathrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647).

`2` keeps homes with two bathrooms or more. Each row reports its own `bathrooms`.
`baths_min` greater than `baths_max` is a 400. Residential sections only  - 
few commercial listings state bathrooms, so on commercial it would exclude the rest.

baths_max.description:

`1` keeps homes with at most one bathroom. Pair with `baths_min` for an exact count (`baths_min=2&baths_max=2`).

floor_area_min.description:
**Smallest floor area, in square feet.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

- `500`  -  excludes most studios.
- `1000`  -  a family home.
- `5000`  -  large commercial units.

Square feet, not square metres (1 m² ≈ 10.76 sq ft). Listings with no published size are excluded
once a size bound is set. Each row carries `floor_area_sqft` and `floor_area_source`.

floor_area_max.description:
**Largest floor area, in square feet.** Optional; no ceiling when omitted.

`800` keeps homes of 800 sq ft or less. Send with `floor_area_min` for a window; `floor_area_min` greater
than `floor_area_max` is a 400. At least `1` (a `0` ceiling is read as none, so it is refused).

property_type.description:
**Kind of property.** Optional; one value or several comma-separated  -  **several are combined (any of
them)**, e.g. `detached,semi_detached` or `industrial,warehouse`.

**Residential sections** (`for-sale`, `to-rent`, `new-homes`):

- `houses`  -  detached, semi-detached and terraced; or `detached`, `semi_detached`, `terraced` alone
  (detached bungalows count as detached).
- `bungalow`, or the finer `detached_bungalow`, `semi_detached_bungalow`, `terraced_bungalow`.
- `cottage`, `barn_conversion`.
- `flats`  -  flats, apartments and maisonettes; `studio`  -  studio flats only.
- `park_home`  -  park and mobile homes; `land`  -  land and plots; `farms_land`  -  land plus farms.
- `hotel`, `hospitality`, `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `retail`, `offices`, `industrial`, `light_industrial`,
  `warehouse`  -  a hotel, shop or office sold or let with living space.

**Commercial sections:**

- `offices`, `serviced_office` (part of `offices`), `retail` (shops).
- `hospitality` (restaurants, pubs, hotels, leisure), or `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `hotel` alone.
- `industrial`, `light_industrial`, `warehouse`; `land`, `farms_land` (land and sites).

A value outside the section's list is a 400 naming the accepted ones. Leisure units, car parking and
business parks have no filter of their own.

tenure.description:

them)**, e.g. `freehold,share_of_freehold`. Sale sections (`for-sale`, `new-homes`, `commercial-for-sale`)
and commercial lettings (a lease offered for assignment).

- `freehold`  -  freehold.
- `leasehold`  -  leasehold.
- `share_of_freehold`  -  share of freehold.
- `commonhold`  -  commonhold (rare).
- `feudal`  -  Scottish feudal tenure (rare).

Listings that state no tenure are excluded once this is set. An unknown value is a 400.

- `unfurnished`  -  unfurnished.

Omit it for all. Listings that state no furnishing are excluded once this is set.

rental_term.description:
**Length of let, for rentals.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

- `long_term`  -  long lets.
- `short_term`  -  short lets, holiday and corporate lets.

Most rentals state no term and are excluded once this is set, so the two values together cover
only a minority of listings.

added.description:
**Only listings (re)published within this window.** Optional.

- `24_hours`  -  the last day.
- `3_days`  -  the last three days.
- `7_days`  -  the last week.
- `14_days`  -  the last fortnight.
- `30_days`  -  the last month.

**The window is on the listing's latest publication, not its first**: a listing back on the market
or refreshed today matches `24_hours` even if it was first listed months ago. Rows carry both `first_published` and `last_published`.
The stateless way to watch an area for new stock.

keywords.description:
**Words that must appear in the listing's own text.** Optional; up to 300 characters (longer is a 400),
e.g. `garage`, `garden`, `penthouse`.

- **Several words must all match:** `garage garden` keeps listings mentioning both.
- **A quoted phrase matches exactly:** `"roof terrace"`.
- **A leading `-` excludes a word:** `-garage` keeps every listing not mentioning a garage.
- **Whole words only:** `garag` matches nothing; a word that appears nowhere returns `total: 0`.
- **As on zoopla.co.uk, `&` and `#` end the text:** `garden & garage` searches `garden`.
- **`+` is a space and a `%` escape is read decoded** (`%20` is a space, `caf%C3%A9` is `café`); any
  other `%` is searched as typed.

smart_tags.description:
**Feature tags the listing must carry.** Optional; comma-separated, e.g.
`attributes.en_suite,attributes.patio`. Every section (on commercial property `style.modern`,
`architecture.period_property`, `attributes.basement` and `attributes.ev_charging` are the useful ones).

- `condition.needs_modernisation`
- `architecture.period_property`
- `type.cottage`
- `style.modern`
- `attributes.ev_charging`
- `attributes.utility_room`
- `attributes.basement`
- `attributes.conservatory`
- `attributes.home_office`
- `attributes.en_suite`
- `attributes.bath`
- `attributes.patio`
- `attributes.kitchen_island`

Also read, though Zoopla's own tag list leaves them out (`/smart-tags` → `unlisted`):

- `attributes.garden`
- `attributes.garage`
- `attributes.balcony`
- `attributes.driveway`

**Several tags are an intersection (AND)**: `attributes.en_suite,attributes.patio` keeps only listings
carrying both. `/smart-tags` lists the tags with their labels. An unknown tag is a 400 naming the accepted ones.

feature.description:
**"Must-have" features.** Optional; comma-separated; **several must all apply**. Every section.

- `has_garden` · `has_parking_garage`
- `has_balcony_terrace` · `has_porter_security`
- `has_fireplace` · `has_wood_floors`

`has_garden,has_parking_garage` keeps only listings with both. Complements `smart_tags` (tags Zoopla
derives from the listing text). An unknown value is a 400 naming the accepted ones.

buyer_incentive.description:
**Buyer incentive schemes.** Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`; comma-separated  -  several are
combined (any of them).

- `shared_ownership`  -  shared-ownership homes (the same set as `is_shared_ownership=true`).
- `help_to_buy`  -  homes still advertised with Help to Buy (a handful; the scheme has closed).
- `shared_equity`  -  shared-equity schemes (a handful).

Any other value is a 400.

radius.description:
**Widen the search to this many miles around the location.** Optional; one of
`0.25`, `0.5`, `1`, `3`, `5`, `10`, `15`, `20`, `30`, `40`.

Works on every kind of location and adds the surrounding area to it: `location_id=m19&radius=1` searches
the district plus about a mile around it, so `total` grows with the radius. The radius applied shows in the answer's `search_url` (`…/manchester/?radius=5`).
Stations and schools are searched as a ½-mile circle by default. `1.0` or `.5` read as `1` / `0.5`; other
distances are a 400  -  they are not offered (for any radius around a point use /search-by-coordinates).

chain_free.description:
**Only chain-free homes** (no onward purchase to wait on). Optional; `for-sale` and `commercial-for-sale`.

`true`  -  chain-free only (every new-build counts as chain free). `false` is the same as leaving it out.
On `section=new-homes` it is not accepted (all qualify).

include_sold.description:
**Also include homes under offer or sold subject to contract.** Optional; sale sections only.

By default only available homes are listed. `true` adds the under-offer / sold-STC ones; their `flag`/`tags` show the status. `false` is the same as leaving it out.

include_rented.description:
**Also include rentals already let agreed.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

By default only available rentals are listed. `true` adds the let-agreed ones. `false` is the same as
leaving it out.

is_auction.description:
**Auction lots.** Optional; sale sections only.

`true`  -  auction lots only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_retirement_home.description:
**Retirement homes.** Optional; `for-sale`, `new-homes` and `to-rent`.

`true`  -  retirement properties only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_shared_ownership.description:
**Shared-ownership homes** (buy a share, rent the rest). Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`.

`true`  -  shared ownership only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_shared_accommodation.description:
**Rooms in shared houses and flat shares.** Optional; `section=to-rent` only.

`true`  -  shared accommodation only. `false`  -  **excludes** it. Omit it for both.

is_student_accommodation.description:
**Student accommodation.** Optional; `section=to-rent` only.

`true`  -  student lets only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

reduced_price_only.description:
**Price-reduced listings.** Optional; every section.

`true`  -  only listings whose price has been cut. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Rows carry `price_drop_percent` and `last_price_change`.

bills_included.description:
**Rentals with bills included in the rent.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`
(on commercial lettings, chiefly serviced offices).

`true`  -  bills included. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

pets_allowed.description:
**Rentals that accept pets.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

`true`  -  pets allowed (most listings do not say, so this keeps few). `false` is the same as leaving it
out  -  it does not find pet-free lets.

new_homes.description:
**New-build homes within a for-sale search.** Optional; `section=for-sale` only.

`true`  -  new builds only (the same set as `section=new-homes`). `false`  -  **excludes** new builds (the
resale market). Omit it for both.

is_development.description:
**Homes in a new development** (a multi-unit scheme). Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`.

`true`  -  development plots only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

sort.description:
**Result order.** Optional; default `newest_listings`.

- `newest_listings`  -  newest first by Zoopla's own listing date; rows are not in strict `last_published`
  order, so do not rely on it to sort by that field.
- `highest_price`  -  most expensive first.
- `lowest_price`  -  cheapest first.
- `most_reduced`  -  biggest price cuts first.

Featured listings (`featured`) are placed by Zoopla and do not follow the sort.

page.description:
**Which page of 25 results to return.** Optional; default `1`, at most `40`.

**A search hands back at most 40 pages × 25 = 1,000 listings, whatever its `total`.** Each
answer says so: `retrievable_total` (= the smaller of `total` and 1,000), `total_pages` (≤ 40) and
`has_more`. When `total_is_capped` is `true`, `total` itself is a floor (it stops counting at 50,000).
To collect more than 1,000, split the search into slices under 1,000 each  -  price bands work best  - 
and page each slice. A page past 40 is a 400.

description: Search listings within any radius (0.1 - 40 miles) of a UK map point, with the full filter set, sorts and pages of 25; every row carries its distance.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the point, in decimal degrees.** Required; UK only  -  `49` to `61`.

`51.5074` is central London, `53.4808` central Manchester, `55.9533` Edinburgh. Pair it with
`longitude`. A point outside the UK box, or in the Republic of Ireland or France (both inside it)  -  on land or
in their waters: the Irish half of the Irish Sea, and the sea within a few km of the French coast  -  is a 400; a
blank value is a 400, never read as `0`.

`5` a town. Every listing returned lies inside the circle (each row's `distance_miles` is at most
the radius), and the answer's `centre.radius_miles` echoes it.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description:
**Which market to search.** Optional; default `for-sale`.

- `for-sale`  -  homes for sale (the default).
- `to-rent`  -  homes to rent.
- `new-homes`  -  new-build homes for sale (every new home counts as chain free).
- `commercial-for-sale`  -  commercial property for sale (offices, shops, hospitality, industrial, land).
- `commercial-to-rent`  -  commercial property to let.

**Filters are per section**  -  one outside its section is a 400 naming the sections that take it:

- **Every section:** price, floor area, `property_type`, `keywords`, `added`, `smart_tags`, `feature`,
  `reduced_price_only`; `radius` for a named place.
- **Residential:** bedrooms and bathrooms.
- **Sale:** `tenure`, `include_sold`, `is_auction`; `chain_free` (not `new-homes`); `is_shared_ownership`,
  `is_retirement_home`, `is_development`, `buyer_incentive` (`for-sale`, `new-homes`); `new_homes` (`for-sale`).
- **Letting:** `price_frequency`, `furnished_state`, `rental_term`, `include_rented`, `bills_included`,
  `pets_allowed`, `available_now`; `is_shared_accommodation`, `is_student_accommodation`, `is_retirement_home`
  (`to-rent`); `tenure` (`commercial-to-rent`).

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description:
**Lowest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `200000`  -  £200k and up for sale.
- `1000`  -  £1,000 a month and up to rent.

Both bounds are inclusive. `price_min` greater than `price_max` is a 400. Every row carries its numeric `price`, so the bound can be checked row by row (POA listings have `price: null`).

**Highest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no ceiling when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

is refused rather than silently returning everything.

parameters.name: price_frequency

**The unit `price_min` / `price_max` are read in, for rentals.** Optional; default `per_month`.

- `per_month`  -  monthly rent (pcm).

- `per_year`  -  annual rent (pa), how commercial rents are usually quoted: `price_max=12000&price_frequency=per_year`

It changes only how the price bounds are read  -  rows still show each listing's own advertised price and `price_frequency`. Accepted with `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent` only.

- `0`  -  studios included (it still drops the few listings that state no bedroom count).
- `3`  -  three bedrooms or more.
- `11`  -  eleven or more.

Each row reports its own `bedrooms`. `beds_min` greater than `beds_max` is a 400. Not accepted on
commercial sections: almost no commercial listing states bedrooms, so it would exclude nearly all of them.

parameters.name: property_type
parameters.description:
**Kind of property.** Optional; one value or several comma-separated  -  **several are combined (any of
them)**, e.g. `detached,semi_detached` or `industrial,warehouse`.

**Residential sections** (`for-sale`, `to-rent`, `new-homes`):

- `houses`  -  detached, semi-detached and terraced; or `detached`, `semi_detached`, `terraced` alone
  (detached bungalows count as detached).
- `bungalow`, or the finer `detached_bungalow`, `semi_detached_bungalow`, `terraced_bungalow`.
- `cottage`, `barn_conversion`.
- `flats`  -  flats, apartments and maisonettes; `studio`  -  studio flats only.
- `park_home`  -  park and mobile homes; `land`  -  land and plots; `farms_land`  -  land plus farms.
- `hotel`, `hospitality`, `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `retail`, `offices`, `industrial`, `light_industrial`,
  `warehouse`  -  a hotel, shop or office sold or let with living space.

**Commercial sections:**

- `offices`, `serviced_office` (part of `offices`), `retail` (shops).
- `hospitality` (restaurants, pubs, hotels, leisure), or `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `hotel` alone.
- `industrial`, `light_industrial`, `warehouse`; `land`, `farms_land` (land and sites).

A value outside the section's list is a 400 naming the accepted ones. Leisure units, car parking and
business parks have no filter of their own.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description:
**Words that must appear in the listing's own text.** Optional; up to 300 characters (longer is a 400),
e.g. `garage`, `garden`, `penthouse`.

- **Several words must all match:** `garage garden` keeps listings mentioning both.
- **A quoted phrase matches exactly:** `"roof terrace"`.
- **A leading `-` excludes a word:** `-garage` keeps every listing not mentioning a garage.
- **Whole words only:** `garag` matches nothing; a word that appears nowhere returns `total: 0`.
- **As on zoopla.co.uk, `&` and `#` end the text:** `garden & garage` searches `garden`.
- **`+` is a space and a `%` escape is read decoded** (`%20` is a space, `caf%C3%A9` is `café`); any
  other `%` is searched as typed.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
**Which page of 25 results to return.** Optional; default `1`, at most `40`.

**A search hands back at most 40 pages × 25 = 1,000 listings, whatever its `total`.** Each
answer says so: `retrievable_total` (= the smaller of `total` and 1,000), `total_pages` (≤ 40) and
`has_more`. When `total_is_capped` is `true`, `total` itself is a floor (it stops counting at 50,000).
To collect more than 1,000, split the search into slices under 1,000 each  -  price bands work best  - 
and page each slice. A page past 40 is a 400.

latitude.description:
**Latitude of the point, in decimal degrees.** Required; UK only  -  `49` to `61`.

`51.5074` is central London, `53.4808` central Manchester, `55.9533` Edinburgh. Pair it with
`longitude`. A point outside the UK box, or in the Republic of Ireland or France (both inside it)  -  on land or
in their waters: the Irish half of the Irish Sea, and the sea within a few km of the French coast  -  is a 400; a
blank value is a 400, never read as `0`.

longitude.description:
**Longitude of the point, in decimal degrees.** Required; UK only  -  `-9` to `2.5`.

Most of Great Britain is **west of Greenwich, so negative**: `-0.1278` central London, `-2.2426`
Manchester, `-3.1883` Edinburgh; East Anglia and Kent are small positives (`1.2974` Norwich). A point
outside the UK box, or in the Republic of Ireland or France (on land or in their waters), is a 400.

radius.description:
**Radius of the circle around the point, in miles.** Optional; default `1`, from `0.1` to `40`.

Any value in the range works, fractions included  -  `0.25` is a few streets, `1` a neighbourhood,
`5` a town. Every listing returned lies inside the circle (each row's `distance_miles` is at most
the radius), and the answer's `centre.radius_miles` echoes it.

section.description:
**Which market to search.** Optional; default `for-sale`.

- `for-sale`  -  homes for sale (the default).
- `to-rent`  -  homes to rent.
- `new-homes`  -  new-build homes for sale (every new home counts as chain free).
- `commercial-for-sale`  -  commercial property for sale (offices, shops, hospitality, industrial, land).
- `commercial-to-rent`  -  commercial property to let.

**Filters are per section**  -  one outside its section is a 400 naming the sections that take it:

- **Every section:** price, floor area, `property_type`, `keywords`, `added`, `smart_tags`, `feature`,
  `reduced_price_only`; `radius` for a named place.
- **Residential:** bedrooms and bathrooms.
- **Sale:** `tenure`, `include_sold`, `is_auction`; `chain_free` (not `new-homes`); `is_shared_ownership`,
  `is_retirement_home`, `is_development`, `buyer_incentive` (`for-sale`, `new-homes`); `new_homes` (`for-sale`).
- **Letting:** `price_frequency`, `furnished_state`, `rental_term`, `include_rented`, `bills_included`,
  `pets_allowed`, `available_now`; `is_shared_accommodation`, `is_student_accommodation`, `is_retirement_home`
  (`to-rent`); `tenure` (`commercial-to-rent`).

price_min.description:
**Lowest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `200000`  -  £200k and up for sale.
- `1000`  -  £1,000 a month and up to rent.

Both bounds are inclusive. `price_min` greater than `price_max` is a 400. Every row carries its numeric `price`, so the bound can be checked row by row (POA listings have `price: null`).

price_max.description:
**Highest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no ceiling when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `300000`  -  up to £300k for sale.
- `1200`  -  up to £1,200 a month to rent (`1200` with `price_frequency=per_week` means £1,200 a week).

Send it with `price_min` for a band. Price bands are also the best way to split a big search into
slices of under 1,000 listings each (see `page`). At least `1`: Zoopla reads `0` as no ceiling, so it
is refused rather than silently returning everything.

price_frequency.description:
**The unit `price_min` / `price_max` are read in, for rentals.** Optional; default `per_month`.

- `per_month`  -  monthly rent (pcm).
- `per_week`  -  weekly rent (pw): `price_max=250&price_frequency=per_week` ≈ £1,083 a month.
- `per_year`  -  annual rent (pa), how commercial rents are usually quoted: `price_max=12000&price_frequency=per_year`
  = £1,000 a month.

It changes only how the price bounds are read  -  rows still show each listing's own advertised price and `price_frequency`. Accepted with `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent` only.

beds_min.description:
**Fewest bedrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647). Residential sections only.

- `0`  -  studios included (it still drops the few listings that state no bedroom count).
- `3`  -  three bedrooms or more.
- `11`  -  eleven or more.

Each row reports its own `bedrooms`. `beds_min` greater than `beds_max` is a 400. Not accepted on
commercial sections: almost no commercial listing states bedrooms, so it would exclude nearly all of them.

beds_max.description:
**Most bedrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647), except `10`.

- `0`  -  studios, plus any room let listed with `0` bedrooms.
- `2`  -  up to two bedrooms.

Send with `beds_min` for an exact count (`beds_min=2&beds_max=2`). `10` is a 400: Zoopla reads it as its
"10+" option (no ceiling), so no value caps a search at exactly 10  -  send `9` or `11`. Not accepted on
commercial sections.

baths_min.description:
**Fewest bathrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647).

`2` keeps homes with two bathrooms or more. Each row reports its own `bathrooms`.
`baths_min` greater than `baths_max` is a 400. Residential sections only  - 
few commercial listings state bathrooms, so on commercial it would exclude the rest.

baths_max.description:
**Most bathrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647).

`1` keeps homes with at most one bathroom. Pair with `baths_min` for an exact count (`baths_min=2&baths_max=2`).
Residential sections only.

floor_area_min.description:
**Smallest floor area, in square feet.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

- `500`  -  excludes most studios.
- `1000`  -  a family home.
- `5000`  -  large commercial units.

Square feet, not square metres (1 m² ≈ 10.76 sq ft). Listings with no published size are excluded
once a size bound is set. Each row carries `floor_area_sqft` and `floor_area_source`.

floor_area_max.description:
**Largest floor area, in square feet.** Optional; no ceiling when omitted.

`800` keeps homes of 800 sq ft or less. Send with `floor_area_min` for a window; `floor_area_min` greater
than `floor_area_max` is a 400. At least `1` (a `0` ceiling is read as none, so it is refused).

property_type.description:
**Kind of property.** Optional; one value or several comma-separated  -  **several are combined (any of
them)**, e.g. `detached,semi_detached` or `industrial,warehouse`.

**Residential sections** (`for-sale`, `to-rent`, `new-homes`):

- `houses`  -  detached, semi-detached and terraced; or `detached`, `semi_detached`, `terraced` alone
  (detached bungalows count as detached).
- `bungalow`, or the finer `detached_bungalow`, `semi_detached_bungalow`, `terraced_bungalow`.
- `cottage`, `barn_conversion`.
- `flats`  -  flats, apartments and maisonettes; `studio`  -  studio flats only.
- `park_home`  -  park and mobile homes; `land`  -  land and plots; `farms_land`  -  land plus farms.
- `hotel`, `hospitality`, `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `retail`, `offices`, `industrial`, `light_industrial`,
  `warehouse`  -  a hotel, shop or office sold or let with living space.

**Commercial sections:**

- `offices`, `serviced_office` (part of `offices`), `retail` (shops).
- `hospitality` (restaurants, pubs, hotels, leisure), or `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `hotel` alone.
- `industrial`, `light_industrial`, `warehouse`; `land`, `farms_land` (land and sites).

A value outside the section's list is a 400 naming the accepted ones. Leisure units, car parking and
business parks have no filter of their own.

- `share_of_freehold`  -  share of freehold.

keywords.description:
**Words that must appear in the listing's own text.** Optional; up to 300 characters (longer is a 400),
e.g. `garage`, `garden`, `penthouse`.

- **Several words must all match:** `garage garden` keeps listings mentioning both.
- **A quoted phrase matches exactly:** `"roof terrace"`.
- **A leading `-` excludes a word:** `-garage` keeps every listing not mentioning a garage.
- **Whole words only:** `garag` matches nothing; a word that appears nowhere returns `total: 0`.
- **As on zoopla.co.uk, `&` and `#` end the text:** `garden & garage` searches `garden`.
- **`+` is a space and a `%` escape is read decoded** (`%20` is a space, `caf%C3%A9` is `café`); any
  other `%` is searched as typed.

smart_tags.description:
**Feature tags the listing must carry.** Optional; comma-separated, e.g.
`attributes.en_suite,attributes.patio`. Every section (on commercial property `style.modern`,
`architecture.period_property`, `attributes.basement` and `attributes.ev_charging` are the useful ones).

- `condition.needs_modernisation`
- `architecture.period_property`
- `type.cottage`
- `style.modern`
- `attributes.ev_charging`
- `attributes.utility_room`
- `attributes.basement`
- `attributes.conservatory`
- `attributes.home_office`
- `attributes.en_suite`
- `attributes.bath`
- `attributes.patio`
- `attributes.kitchen_island`

Also read, though Zoopla's own tag list leaves them out (`/smart-tags` → `unlisted`):

- `attributes.garden`
- `attributes.garage`
- `attributes.balcony`
- `attributes.driveway`

**Several tags are an intersection (AND)**: `attributes.en_suite,attributes.patio` keeps only listings
carrying both. `/smart-tags` lists the tags with their labels. An unknown tag is a 400 naming the accepted ones.

feature.description:
**"Must-have" features.** Optional; comma-separated; **several must all apply**. Every section.

- `has_garden` · `has_parking_garage`
- `has_balcony_terrace` · `has_porter_security`
- `has_fireplace` · `has_wood_floors`

`has_garden,has_parking_garage` keeps only listings with both. Complements `smart_tags` (tags Zoopla
derives from the listing text). An unknown value is a 400 naming the accepted ones.

buyer_incentive.description:
**Buyer incentive schemes.** Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`; comma-separated  -  several are
combined (any of them).

- `shared_ownership`  -  shared-ownership homes (the same set as `is_shared_ownership=true`).
- `help_to_buy`  -  homes still advertised with Help to Buy (a handful; the scheme has closed).
- `shared_equity`  -  shared-equity schemes (a handful).

Any other value is a 400.

chain_free.description:
**Only chain-free homes** (no onward purchase to wait on). Optional; `for-sale` and `commercial-for-sale`.

`true`  -  chain-free only (every new-build counts as chain free). `false` is the same as leaving it out.
On `section=new-homes` it is not accepted (all qualify).

include_sold.description:
**Also include homes under offer or sold subject to contract.** Optional; sale sections only.

By default only available homes are listed. `true` adds the under-offer / sold-STC ones; their `flag`/`tags` show the status. `false` is the same as leaving it out.

include_rented.description:
**Also include rentals already let agreed.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

By default only available rentals are listed. `true` adds the let-agreed ones. `false` is the same as
leaving it out.

is_auction.description:
**Auction lots.** Optional; sale sections only.

`true`  -  auction lots only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_retirement_home.description:
**Retirement homes.** Optional; `for-sale`, `new-homes` and `to-rent`.

`true`  -  retirement properties only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_shared_ownership.description:
**Shared-ownership homes** (buy a share, rent the rest). Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`.

`true`  -  shared ownership only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_shared_accommodation.description:
**Rooms in shared houses and flat shares.** Optional; `section=to-rent` only.

`true`  -  shared accommodation only. `false`  -  **excludes** it. Omit it for both.

is_student_accommodation.description:
**Student accommodation.** Optional; `section=to-rent` only.

`true`  -  student lets only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

reduced_price_only.description:
**Price-reduced listings.** Optional; every section.

`true`  -  only listings whose price has been cut. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Rows carry `price_drop_percent` and `last_price_change`.

bills_included.description:
**Rentals with bills included in the rent.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`
(on commercial lettings, chiefly serviced offices).

`true`  -  bills included. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

pets_allowed.description:
**Rentals that accept pets.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

`true`  -  pets allowed (most listings do not say, so this keeps few). `false` is the same as leaving it
out  -  it does not find pet-free lets.

new_homes.description:
**New-build homes within a for-sale search.** Optional; `section=for-sale` only.

`true`  -  new builds only (the same set as `section=new-homes`). `false`  -  **excludes** new builds (the
resale market). Omit it for both.

is_development.description:
**Homes in a new development** (a multi-unit scheme). Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`.

`true`  -  development plots only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

sort.description:
**Result order.** Optional; default `newest_listings`.

- `newest_listings`  -  newest first by Zoopla's own listing date; rows are not in strict `last_published`
  order, so do not rely on it to sort by that field.
- `highest_price`  -  most expensive first.
- `lowest_price`  -  cheapest first.
- `most_reduced`  -  biggest price cuts first.

Featured listings (`featured`) are placed by Zoopla and do not follow the sort.

page.description:
**Which page of 25 results to return.** Optional; default `1`, at most `40`.

**A search hands back at most 40 pages × 25 = 1,000 listings, whatever its `total`.** Each
answer says so: `retrievable_total` (= the smaller of `total` and 1,000), `total_pages` (≤ 40) and
`has_more`. When `total_is_capped` is `true`, `total` itself is a floor (it stops counting at 50,000).
To collect more than 1,000, split the search into slices under 1,000 each  -  price bands work best  - 
and page each slice. A page past 40 is a 400.

description: Paste a Zoopla search results page address and get its listings, with the URL's section, place and filters echoed back.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description:
**A Zoopla search results page address.** Required  -  paste it as it appears in the browser, with or
without `https://`, `www.` and its query string.

**Accepted:** search pages of every section (`/for-sale/property/manchester/`, `/to-rent/commercial/offices/london/`)
and the path forms the site links to  -  a type (`/for-sale/houses/bristol/`), an include word (`shared-ownership`,
`retirement`, `auction`, `student-accommodation`), a bedroom count (`/flats/2-bedrooms/`, `/studio/`) and the
map view `/for-sale/map/property/…` (`polyenc`).

**Read exactly as zoopla.co.uk reads it:**

- The query's filters, repeated values and `pn` (the page) apply; one commercial `property_sub_type`
  under /for-sale/ or /to-rent/ makes it the commercial search.
- A path type counts only as the first word; so do `shared-ownership` and `student-accommodation` (later
  in the path, a 404), and a query `property_sub_type` overrides those two.
- Names and values are case-sensitive; on two-state flags any value but `true` reads as `false`, and the
  older `include_auctions`-style keys read only `false`.

**`parsed.ignored_params`** lists what was not applied: unread names (`q`, `utm_*`), ignored values as
`name=value` (`radius=7`, `price_max=0`) and unread path words as `path:`.

**400:** a value the search would fail on (e.g. `tenure`, `smart_tags`, `polyenc`, a `pn` outside 1 - 40),
a parameter repeated with two different values, the older `/commercial/for-sale/…` form, a listing page
(use `/listing-by-url`), or a house-prices, agent, developer, guide or non-Zoopla page.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.description:
**The estate-agent (or developer) branch.** Required.

A branch id is on every `/agents` and `/agents-near` row (`branch_id`), on every listing row
(`agent.branch_id` in `/search`, `/listing-details`, …) and on every `/new-home-developments` row (a
development is a developer branch). It is also the number at the end of a Zoopla agent page address
(`…/find-agents/branch/goldschmidt-and-howland-hampstead-lettings-london-14416/` → `14416`).

An id that is not a Zoopla branch is a **404**.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description:
**Which market to search.** Optional; default `for-sale`.

- `for-sale`  -  homes for sale (the default).
- `to-rent`  -  homes to rent.
- `new-homes`  -  new-build homes for sale (every new home counts as chain free).
- `commercial-for-sale`  -  commercial property for sale (offices, shops, hospitality, industrial, land).
- `commercial-to-rent`  -  commercial property to let.

**Filters are per section**  -  one outside its section is a 400 naming the sections that take it:

- **Every section:** price, floor area, `property_type`, `keywords`, `added`, `smart_tags`, `feature`,
  `reduced_price_only`; `radius` for a named place.
- **Residential:** bedrooms and bathrooms.
- **Sale:** `tenure`, `include_sold`, `is_auction`; `chain_free` (not `new-homes`); `is_shared_ownership`,
  `is_retirement_home`, `is_development`, `buyer_incentive` (`for-sale`, `new-homes`); `new_homes` (`for-sale`).
- **Letting:** `price_frequency`, `furnished_state`, `rental_term`, `include_rented`, `bills_included`,
  `pets_allowed`, `available_now`; `is_shared_accommodation`, `is_student_accommodation`, `is_retirement_home`
  (`to-rent`); `tenure` (`commercial-to-rent`).

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description:
**Lowest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `200000`  -  £200k and up for sale.
- `1000`  -  £1,000 a month and up to rent.

Both bounds are inclusive. `price_min` greater than `price_max` is a 400. Every row carries its numeric `price`, so the bound can be checked row by row (POA listings have `price: null`).

parameters.description:
**Words that must appear in the listing's own text.** Optional; up to 300 characters (longer is a 400),
e.g. `garage`, `garden`, `penthouse`.

- **Several words must all match:** `garage garden` keeps listings mentioning both.

- **As on zoopla.co.uk, `&` and `#` end the text:** `garden & garage` searches `garden`.
- **`+` is a space and a `%` escape is read decoded** (`%20` is a space, `caf%C3%A9` is `café`); any
  other `%` is searched as typed.

- `commercial-to-rent`  -  commercial property to let.

**Filters are per section**  -  one outside its section is a 400 naming the sections that take it:

- **Every section:** price, floor area, `property_type`, `keywords`, `added`, `smart_tags`, `feature`,
  `reduced_price_only`; `radius` for a named place.
- **Residential:** bedrooms and bathrooms.

price_min.description:
**Lowest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no floor when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `200000`  -  £200k and up for sale.
- `1000`  -  £1,000 a month and up to rent.

Both bounds are inclusive. `price_min` greater than `price_max` is a 400. Every row carries its numeric `price`, so the bound can be checked row by row (POA listings have `price: null`).

price_max.description:
**Highest price to include, in whole pounds.** Optional; no ceiling when omitted.

Whole pounds (GBP). For sale: the asking price. To rent (homes and commercial): the rent **per month** by
default, or per week / per year with `price_frequency=per_week` / `per_year`.

- `300000`  -  up to £300k for sale.
- `1200`  -  up to £1,200 a month to rent (`1200` with `price_frequency=per_week` means £1,200 a week).

Send it with `price_min` for a band. Price bands are also the best way to split a big search into
slices of under 1,000 listings each (see `page`). At least `1`: Zoopla reads `0` as no ceiling, so it
is refused rather than silently returning everything.

price_frequency.description:
**The unit `price_min` / `price_max` are read in, for rentals.** Optional; default `per_month`.

- `per_month`  -  monthly rent (pcm).
- `per_week`  -  weekly rent (pw): `price_max=250&price_frequency=per_week` ≈ £1,083 a month.
- `per_year`  -  annual rent (pa), how commercial rents are usually quoted: `price_max=12000&price_frequency=per_year`
  = £1,000 a month.

It changes only how the price bounds are read  -  rows still show each listing's own advertised price and `price_frequency`. Accepted with `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent` only.

beds_min.description:
**Fewest bedrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647). Residential sections only.

- `0`  -  studios included (it still drops the few listings that state no bedroom count).
- `3`  -  three bedrooms or more.
- `11`  -  eleven or more.

Each row reports its own `bedrooms`. `beds_min` greater than `beds_max` is a 400. Not accepted on
commercial sections: almost no commercial listing states bedrooms, so it would exclude nearly all of them.

beds_max.description:
**Most bedrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647), except `10`.

- `0`  -  studios, plus any room let listed with `0` bedrooms.
- `2`  -  up to two bedrooms.

Send with `beds_min` for an exact count (`beds_min=2&beds_max=2`). `10` is a 400: Zoopla reads it as its
"10+" option (no ceiling), so no value caps a search at exactly 10  -  send `9` or `11`. Not accepted on
commercial sections.

baths_min.description:
**Fewest bathrooms.** Optional; a whole number from `0` (up to 2147483647).

`2` keeps homes with two bathrooms or more. Each row reports its own `bathrooms`.
`baths_min` greater than `baths_max` is a 400. Residential sections only  - 
few commercial listings state bathrooms, so on commercial it would exclude the rest.

floor_area_min.description:

- `1000`  -  a family home.

floor_area_max.description:

**Residential sections** (`for-sale`, `to-rent`, `new-homes`):

- `houses`  -  detached, semi-detached and terraced; or `detached`, `semi_detached`, `terraced` alone
  (detached bungalows count as detached).
- `bungalow`, or the finer `detached_bungalow`, `semi_detached_bungalow`, `terraced_bungalow`.
- `cottage`, `barn_conversion`.
- `flats`  -  flats, apartments and maisonettes; `studio`  -  studio flats only.
- `park_home`  -  park and mobile homes; `land`  -  land and plots; `farms_land`  -  land plus farms.
- `hotel`, `hospitality`, `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `retail`, `offices`, `industrial`, `light_industrial`,
  `warehouse`  -  a hotel, shop or office sold or let with living space.

**Commercial sections:**

- `offices`, `serviced_office` (part of `offices`), `retail` (shops).
- `hospitality` (restaurants, pubs, hotels, leisure), or `restaurant`, `pub_bar`, `hotel` alone.
- `industrial`, `light_industrial`, `warehouse`; `land`, `farms_land` (land and sites).

A value outside the section's list is a 400 naming the accepted ones. Leisure units, car parking and
business parks have no filter of their own.

tenure.description:
**Ownership tenure.** Optional; one value or several comma-separated  -  **several are combined (any of
them)**, e.g. `freehold,share_of_freehold`. Sale sections (`for-sale`, `new-homes`, `commercial-for-sale`)
and commercial lettings (a lease offered for assignment).

- `freehold`  -  freehold.
- `leasehold`  -  leasehold.
- `share_of_freehold`  -  share of freehold.
- `commonhold`  -  commonhold (rare).
- `feudal`  -  Scottish feudal tenure (rare).

Listings that state no tenure are excluded once this is set. An unknown value is a 400.

furnished_state.description:
**Furnishing, for rentals.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

- `furnished`  -  furnished.
- `part_furnished`  -  part furnished.
- `unfurnished`  -  unfurnished.

Omit it for all. Listings that state no furnishing are excluded once this is set.

rental_term.description:
**Length of let, for rentals.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

- `long_term`  -  long lets.
- `short_term`  -  short lets, holiday and corporate lets.

Most rentals state no term and are excluded once this is set, so the two values together cover
only a minority of listings.

added.description:
**Only listings (re)published within this window.** Optional.

- `24_hours`  -  the last day.
- `3_days`  -  the last three days.
- `7_days`  -  the last week.
- `14_days`  -  the last fortnight.
- `30_days`  -  the last month.

**The window is on the listing's latest publication, not its first**: a listing back on the market
or refreshed today matches `24_hours` even if it was first listed months ago. Rows carry both `first_published` and `last_published`.

keywords.description:
**Words that must appear in the listing's own text.** Optional; up to 300 characters (longer is a 400),
e.g. `garage`, `garden`, `penthouse`.

- **Several words must all match:** `garage garden` keeps listings mentioning both.
- **A quoted phrase matches exactly:** `"roof terrace"`.
- **A leading `-` excludes a word:** `-garage` keeps every listing not mentioning a garage.
- **Whole words only:** `garag` matches nothing; a word that appears nowhere returns `total: 0`.
- **As on zoopla.co.uk, `&` and `#` end the text:** `garden & garage` searches `garden`.
- **`+` is a space and a `%` escape is read decoded** (`%20` is a space, `caf%C3%A9` is `café`); any
  other `%` is searched as typed.

smart_tags.description:
**Feature tags the listing must carry.** Optional; comma-separated, e.g.
`attributes.en_suite,attributes.patio`. Every section (on commercial property `style.modern`,
`architecture.period_property`, `attributes.basement` and `attributes.ev_charging` are the useful ones).

- `condition.needs_modernisation`
- `architecture.period_property`
- `type.cottage`
- `style.modern`
- `attributes.ev_charging`
- `attributes.utility_room`
- `attributes.basement`
- `attributes.conservatory`
- `attributes.home_office`
- `attributes.en_suite`
- `attributes.bath`
- `attributes.patio`
- `attributes.kitchen_island`

Also read, though Zoopla's own tag list leaves them out (`/smart-tags` → `unlisted`):

- `attributes.garden`
- `attributes.garage`
- `attributes.balcony`
- `attributes.driveway`

**Several tags are an intersection (AND)**: `attributes.en_suite,attributes.patio` keeps only listings
carrying both. `/smart-tags` lists the tags with their labels. An unknown tag is a 400 naming the accepted ones.

feature.description:
**"Must-have" features.** Optional; comma-separated; **several must all apply**. Every section.

- `has_garden` · `has_parking_garage`
- `has_balcony_terrace` · `has_porter_security`
- `has_fireplace` · `has_wood_floors`

`has_garden,has_parking_garage` keeps only listings with both. Complements `smart_tags` (tags Zoopla
derives from the listing text). An unknown value is a 400 naming the accepted ones.

buyer_incentive.description:
**Buyer incentive schemes.** Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`; comma-separated  -  several are
combined (any of them).

- `shared_ownership`  -  shared-ownership homes (the same set as `is_shared_ownership=true`).
- `help_to_buy`  -  homes still advertised with Help to Buy (a handful; the scheme has closed).
- `shared_equity`  -  shared-equity schemes (a handful).

Any other value is a 400.

chain_free.description:
**Only chain-free homes** (no onward purchase to wait on). Optional; `for-sale` and `commercial-for-sale`.

`true`  -  chain-free only (every new-build counts as chain free). `false` is the same as leaving it out.
On `section=new-homes` it is not accepted (all qualify).

include_sold.description:
**Also include homes under offer or sold subject to contract.** Optional; sale sections only.

By default only available homes are listed. `true` adds the under-offer / sold-STC ones; their `flag`/`tags` show the status. `false` is the same as leaving it out.

include_rented.description:
**Also include rentals already let agreed.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

By default only available rentals are listed. `true` adds the let-agreed ones. `false` is the same as
leaving it out.

is_auction.description:
**Auction lots.** Optional; sale sections only.

`true`  -  auction lots only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_retirement_home.description:
**Retirement homes.** Optional; `for-sale`, `new-homes` and `to-rent`.

`true`  -  retirement properties only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_shared_ownership.description:
**Shared-ownership homes** (buy a share, rent the rest). Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`.

`true`  -  shared ownership only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

is_shared_accommodation.description:
**Rooms in shared houses and flat shares.** Optional; `section=to-rent` only.

`true`  -  shared accommodation only. `false`  -  **excludes** it. Omit it for both.

is_student_accommodation.description:
**Student accommodation.** Optional; `section=to-rent` only.

`true`  -  student lets only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

reduced_price_only.description:
**Price-reduced listings.** Optional; every section.

`true`  -  only listings whose price has been cut. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Rows carry `price_drop_percent` and `last_price_change`.

bills_included.description:
**Rentals with bills included in the rent.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`
(on commercial lettings, chiefly serviced offices).

`true`  -  bills included. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

pets_allowed.description:
**Rentals that accept pets.** Optional; `section=to-rent` and `commercial-to-rent`.

`true`  -  pets allowed (most listings do not say, so this keeps few). `false` is the same as leaving it
out  -  it does not find pet-free lets.

new_homes.description:
**New-build homes within a for-sale search.** Optional; `section=for-sale` only.

`true`  -  new builds only (the same set as `section=new-homes`). `false`  -  **excludes** new builds (the
resale market). Omit it for both.

is_development.description:
**Homes in a new development** (a multi-unit scheme). Optional; `for-sale` and `new-homes`.

`true`  -  development plots only. `false`  -  **excludes** them. Omit it for both.

sort.description:
**Result order.** Optional; default `newest_listings`.

- `newest_listings`  -  newest first by Zoopla's own listing date; rows are not in strict `last_published`
  order, so do not rely on it to sort by that field.
- `highest_price`  -  most expensive first.
- `lowest_price`  -  cheapest first.
- `most_reduced`  -  biggest price cuts first.

page.description:
**Which page of 25 results to return.** Optional; default `1`, at most `40`.

**A search hands back at most 40 pages × 25 = 1,000 listings, whatever its `total`.** Each
answer says so: `retrievable_total` (= the smaller of `total` and 1,000), `total_pages` (≤ 40) and
`has_more`. When `total_is_capped` is `true`, `total` itself is a floor (it stops counting at 50,000).
To collect more than 1,000, split the search into slices under 1,000 each  -  price bands work best  - 
and page each slice. A page past 40 is a 400.

description: Up to 50 Zoopla listing page addresses in one call, each read like /listing-by-url into the /listings-by-ids record; addresses that name no listing are reported, not fatal.

parameters.name: urls
parameters.description:
**The Zoopla listing page addresses to read.** Required; 1 - 50 addresses per call.

- **Each address is read as `/listing-by-url` reads one:** any listing page (sale, rent, new homes,
  commercial, or its contact page), with or without `https://`, `www.`/`m.`, a query string, a `#fragment`
  or the trailing slash, in any case. A `/property-history/…/` page is always read with archived
  listings included.
- **Separate addresses** with commas, spaces, new lines, `;` or `|`. A comma inside a query string or
  `#fragment` splits only when a new address starts right after it (`https://`, `www.`, `/for-sale/…`)  - 
  otherwise what follows stays part of that address (see its `source_url`); put a space before it.
- A list percent-encoded once more (`https%3A%2F%2F…`) is decoded and split the same way.
- Two addresses of the same listing are read once.
- An address naming no listing (a search, development or agent page, another site, a page with no
  listing number, a bare id  -  use `/listings-by-ids`) is reported in `invalid` with the reason instead of
  failing the call.

The example sends two live listing pages plus, on purpose, a past listing (it comes back in `not_found`
with `reason` `expired`) and a search page (it comes back in `invalid`).

description: Up to 25 homes in one call by street address with postcode, each matched like /property-by-address and read as the full /property-details record; unmatched addresses are reported, not fatal.

parameters.name: addresses
parameters.description:
**The homes to look up, as one-line UK addresses with their postcodes.** Required; 1 - 25 distinct addresses per call.

Each address is the house number or name and street plus its **full postcode**, anywhere in the line (`10
Mansfield Road, NW3 2HN`, `Flat 4, 17 South Hill Park, London NW3 2ST`); the town and country may be typed
too. Separate addresses with `|`, `;` or new lines  -  a comma-joined list is also split after each postcode that
ends a part (`10 Mansfield Road, NW3 2HN, Flat 4, 17 South Hill Park, NW3 2ST` is two addresses). Each is
matched at its postcode exactly as `/property-by-address` matches its `address` (numbers matter most  -  include
the flat number for a flat). An address typed twice (the same words and postcode, whatever the case, spacing,
accents or punctuation; `&` and `+` read as `and`) is read once  -  but a `-`, `/` or `.` between two numbers counts
(`13-15 Don Street`, a range, is not `13, 15 Don Street`)  -  and two spellings of one home (`Rd` / `Road`) each
get their row. A line with no full postcode, or only a
postcode, is reported in `invalid`; an address that matches no home is reported in `not_found`  -  neither fails
the call.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description:
**The house number or name and street  -  the first line of the address.** Required, free text, e.g.
`25 South Hill Park`, `Flat 4, 17 South Hill Park` (or `4/17 South Hill Park`), `7A South Hill Park` (= Flat A, 7)
or a house name such as `Church House`.

**Numbers matter most:**

- Every number typed must be in the matched address, so include the flat number for a flat. A house number
  alone never matches a flat in that building (`15` is not `15A`), and a flat number never matches a house of
  that number (`Flat 25, South Hill Park` is not `25 South Hill Park`).
- A flat number without its building number still matches (`Apartment 401, Transport House`)  -  unless
  several buildings there have that flat (`Flat 5, Horton Road`), which is a 404.
- A number inside a numbered range (`22 - 30 Don Street`) matches the range only when no address has the
  number itself, and only on the range’s side of the street; a typed range names that range only
  (`15-17 Church Street` is not `17`; `299 to 301` is `299 - 301`).
- A developer’s plot number (`Plot 5, Teal Close`) is not a house number.

**Forgiven:** case, punctuation, accents, word order, common abbreviations (`Rd`, `Ave`, `Gdns`, `Apt`; `St`
after a street name, Saint before one), floor words (`First Floor Flat` = `1st Floor Flat`, `GFF`), Scottish
flat forms (Edinburgh `3/2` = `3F2` and a bare `1F`; Glasgow `2/1` = `Flat 2/1`; `Flat 2-1` is a flat, never a
range), `Flat 21 Don Street` without its comma, and the town, county and postcode.

**A mismatch:** another street type or name (`117 Upper Road` is not `117 Lower Road`), a number the
address gives to a flat of a named block or a house of a named mews (`60 Upper Street` is not
`60 Tyndale Mansions, Upper Street`), another block code (`Apartment Pm 201` is not `Apartment Ns 201`), or a
house name that differs (`East Lodge` is not `West Lodge`; a leading `The` or Welsh `Y` is part of the name).

**404:** nothing at the postcode matches well enough (e.g. a building number split into flats), text that
fits several homes (a street name alone), two addresses joined by `&`, `+` or `and`, or a Glasgow-style `2/1`
where No. 2 is a building and no other number or building name is typed (the message names its addresses).

- A flat number without its building number still matches (`Apartment 401, Transport House`)  -  unless
  several buildings there have that flat (`Flat 5, Horton Road`), which is a 404.
- A number inside a numbered range (`22 - 30 Don Street`) matches the range only when no address has the
  number itself, and only on the range’s side of the street; a typed range names that range only
  (`15-17 Church Street` is not `17`; `299 to 301` is `299 - 301`).
- A developer’s plot number (`Plot 5, Teal Close`) is not a house number.

**Forgiven:** case, punctuation, accents, word order, common abbreviations (`Rd`, `Ave`, `Gdns`, `Apt`; `St`
after a street name, Saint before one), floor words (`First Floor Flat` = `1st Floor Flat`, `GFF`), Scottish
flat forms (Edinburgh `3/2` = `3F2` and a bare `1F`; Glasgow `2/1` = `Flat 2/1`; `Flat 2-1` is a flat, never a
range), `Flat 21 Don Street` without its comma, and the town, county and postcode.

**A mismatch:** another street type or name (`117 Upper Road` is not `117 Lower Road`), a number the
address gives to a flat of a named block or a house of a named mews (`60 Upper Street` is not
`60 Tyndale Mansions, Upper Street`), another block code (`Apartment Pm 201` is not `Apartment Ns 201`), or a
house name that differs (`East Lodge` is not `West Lodge`; a leading `The` or Welsh `Y` is part of the name).

**404:** nothing at the postcode matches well enough (e.g. a building number split into flats), text that
fits several homes (a street name alone), two addresses joined by `&`, `+` or `and`, or a Glasgow-style `2/1`
where No. 2 is a building and no other number or building name is typed (the message names its addresses).

parameters.name: include_boundary

repeat its outline; `[]` when there is none). Several KB for a district or county.

`2000` keeps developments with a home of 2,000 sq ft or more. Homes with no published size never match. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

floor_area_max.description:
**Only developments with a home of at most this floor area, in square feet.** Optional.

`500` keeps developments with a home of 500 sq ft or less. Homes with no published size never match. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

property_type.description:
**Only developments with a home of this kind.** Optional; one value or several comma-separated  - 
**several are combined (any of them)**, e.g. `detached,terraced`.

- `houses`  -  any house; or `detached`, `semi_detached`, `terraced` alone.
- `flats`  -  flats and apartments; `studio`  -  studio flats only.
- `bungalow`, `detached_bungalow`, `semi_detached_bungalow`, `terraced_bungalow`, `cottage`,
  `barn_conversion`, `park_home`, `land`, `farms_land`  -  rare among new homes.

An unknown value is a 400 naming the accepted ones. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

tenure.description:
**Only developments with a home of this tenure.** Optional; comma-separated, any of them.

`freehold`, `leasehold`, `share_of_freehold`, `commonhold`, `feudal`.
Homes that state no tenure never match. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

added.description:
**Only developments with a home (re)published within this window.** Optional.

`24_hours`, `3_days`, `7_days`, `14_days`, `30_days`  -  on the home's latest
publication, not its first. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

keywords.description:
**Only developments with a home whose listing text has these words.** Optional; up to 300 characters (longer is a 400).

`garden` keeps developments with a home whose text mentions a garden; several words must all match;
`"roof terrace"` (quoted) is an exact phrase; a leading `-` excludes a word. As on zoopla.co.uk, `&` and `#` end the text
(`garden & garage` is `garden`), `+` is a space and a `%` escape such as `%20` is read decoded.
A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

smart_tags.description:
**Only developments with a home carrying these feature tags.** Optional; comma-separated; several
must all apply to the same home. The `/smart-tags` vocabulary, plus `attributes.garden`,
`attributes.garage`, `attributes.balcony`, `attributes.driveway`, e.g. `attributes.balcony,style.modern`.
An unknown tag is a 400. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

feature.description:
**Only developments with a home that has these "must-haves".** Optional; comma-separated; several
must all apply. `has_garden`, `has_parking_garage`, `has_balcony_terrace`,
`has_fireplace`, `has_wood_floors`, `has_porter_security`. An unknown value is a 400. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

buyer_incentive.description:
**Only developments with a home offered under a buyer scheme.** Optional; comma-separated, any of them.

`shared_ownership` (the same set as `is_shared_ownership=true`), `help_to_buy`,
`shared_equity` (few or none  -  the schemes have largely closed). Any other value is a 400. A development is listed when **at least one** of its homes matches; its `homes` preview is not filtered.

is_shared_ownership.description:
**Shared-ownership homes.** Optional.

`true`  -  developments with a shared-ownership home; `false`  -  developments with a home that is NOT
shared ownership (a development selling both kinds is in both). Omit it for all.

is_retirement_home.description:
**Retirement homes.** Optional.

`true`  -  developments with a retirement home; `false`  -  developments with a home
that is not one. Omit it for all.

reduced_price_only.description:
**Price-reduced homes.** Optional.

`true`  -  developments with a home whose price has been cut; `false`  -  developments with a home that
has not been reduced (a development with both is in both). Omit it for all.

radius.description:
**Widen the place by this many miles.** Optional; one of `0.25`, `0.5`, `1`, `3`, `5`, `10`, `15`,
`20`, `30`, `40`.

`location_id=m5&radius=5` adds the developments within five miles of the district to it. `1.0` or `.5` read as `1` /
`0.5`; other distances are a 400.

page.description:
**Which page of 25 developments to return.** Optional; default `1`, at most `40`.

At most 40 pages (1,000 developments) per place  -  the whole UK holds more, so page a region or a
town rather than `uk`. `total`, `retrievable_total`, `total_pages` and `has_more` say how far it goes.
A page past 40 is a 400.

description: One new-build development by id: description, price and bedroom range, up to 24 of its homes with price and tenure, photos, video and nearby schools and stations.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.description:
**The new-homes development.** Required.

A development is a developer branch: its id is the `branch_id` of a `/new-home-developments` row, the
`agent.branch_id` of a `/search` row with `section=new-homes`, or the number at the end of a Zoopla
development page address (`…/new-homes/developers/branch/vita-living-circle-square-manchester-169207/`
→ `169207`). An ordinary estate-agent branch id (from `/agents`) is a **404** pointing to
`/agent-details`; an id that is not a branch at all is a **404** too.

description: The public EV charge points nearest a UK map point (20 by default, up to 100 with max_results), with connectors and distance.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description:
**Latitude of the point, in decimal degrees.** Required; UK only  -  `49` to `61`.

`51.5074` is central London, `53.4808` central Manchester, `55.9533` Edinburgh. Pair it with
`longitude`. A point outside the UK box, or in the Republic of Ireland or France (both inside it)  -  on land or
in their waters: the Irish half of the Irish Sea, and the sea within a few km of the French coast  -  is a 400; a
blank value is a 400, never read as `0`.

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description:
**Longitude of the point, in decimal degrees.** Required; UK only  -  `-9` to `2.5`.

Most of Great Britain is **west of Greenwich, so negative**: `-0.1278` central London, `-2.2426`
Manchester, `-3.1883` Edinburgh; East Anglia and Kent are small positives (`1.2974` Norwich). A point
outside the UK box, or in the Republic of Ireland or France (on land or in their waters), is a 400.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description:
**How many charge points to return, nearest first.** Optional; default `20`, `1` - `100`.

There is no radius: the answer is always the N nearest devices, however far  -  a larger number reaches
further out where charge points are sparse. Read each row's `distance_miles`.
